name: Vail / Beaver Creek / Avon, CO
summary: Lionshead in Vail fits this party well. Condo lodges such as Antlers at Vail and Lion Square Lodge rent separate condos or true lock-off suites in one building, about 150 yards from the gondola and roughly 18 restaurants. The animal options are all domestic animals: guided trail rides at Vail Stables (8 minutes) and Beaver Creek Stables (20 minutes), a llama-packed hike with Paragon Guides, and goat yoga or goat feeding at Vail Stables. The municipal Vail Golf Club along Gore Creek is 8 minutes from Lionshead. Antlers quotes US$1,167/night for the trip dates (3BR + 1BR, advance purchase), well under the cap; most other lodges sell the needed units by phone only. The gathering room is always a condo living room whose table size is not stated. The town also sleeps at about 8,150 ft, which matters for travelers aged 79 and 82, and July highs average 76.7 F with about 10 rain days.

brochure.tagline: Gondola rides, goat yoga and creekside strolls in a car-free mountain village
brochure.intro: A week in Vail is easy walks along Gore Creek, gondola rides above the village and dinner on a patio in Lionshead. Mornings can mean a trail ride or a goat visit, afternoons a round of golf or the gardens. Nights are cool, so evenings outside are comfortable.

Feed goats or try goat yoga at Vail Stables

Golf along Gore Creek, 8 minutes from Lionshead
Free in-town bus and walkable creekside villages
pros: Walkable, car-free villages with short, flat strolls

Cool July nights and mountain views
Eagle airport is about 40 minutes away
cons: Town sits at about 8,150 ft; worth a word with doctors

things_to_do.blurb: A guided, family-paced hike in the wilderness near Vail while pack llamas carry the food and gear (June to early September).

things_to_do.name: Vail Golf Club
things_to_do.blurb: An 18-hole public course along Gore Creek with Gore Range views, 8 minutes from Lionshead; EagleVail is a second choice.

things_to_do.blurb: Ride up from Vail Village or Lionshead for mountain views; the gondolas are wheelchair and stroller accessible.

things_to_do.name: Mountain biking
things_to_do.blurb: A signature summer activity in Vail, good for the teens and anyone who likes to be active.

hard_constraints.notes: Airport: Eagle County Regional (EGE) is 37 miles from Vail, about 40 minutes by car, with year-round United/United Express service to Denver; DEN itself is about 2 hours by I-70. Seniors: Lionshead and Vail Village are pedestrian villages along Gore Creek with short walks, and the recommended Antlers Unit 104 is on the first floor. Lion Square, Manor Vail and Beaver Creek Lodge do not state elevators or floors. The town sits at about 8,150-8,240 ft; altitude is a health consideration for travelers aged 79 and 82 but not a staircase or walking problem.

rationale.lodging: 17/25: rests on Antlers at Vail Unit 104 (3BR/2BA category, first floor on request) plus a separate 1BR + bunk condo, $1,167/night before tax (verified 2026-11-14 and re-read 2026-11-15, Advanced Purchase; $1,351 flexible), well inside the cap; points lost because the gathering room is a 1,400 sq ft condo with table size not stated.
rationale.town_scenery: 16/18: Lionshead and Vail Village are car-free creekside villages under Vail Mountain with flat short walks, joined by a roughly 15-minute path or the free bus; some village streets have gentle grades.
rationale.animals: 11/18: the top two items are guided horseback trail rides (Vail Stables, 8 min, 5+; Beaver Creek Stables, 20 min, 7+), a top-tier activity but with farm animals; below them are goat yoga and goat feeding (touching) and a llama-packed hike (close viewing), with no wild or exotic animal encounter.
rationale.food: 14/15: Discover Vail lists 18 Lionshead restaurants within a few minutes' walk of Antlers, and Michelin-recommended Sweet Basil is about 15 minutes away on foot in Vail Village; reservations are hard in July.
rationale.other: 8/10: gondolas, Betty Ford Alpine Gardens, Sunday farmers' market, 12 spas and mountain biking cover most interests; EGE is 40 min with United DEN service, but the Bay Area pair likely connects or drives from DEN, and no escape room or bingo was confirmed.
rationale.golf: 7/9: public Vail Golf Club (par 71 along Gore Creek with Gore Range views, reopens May 2027) is 8 min away and EagleVail is the alternative; green fees unpublished and Red Sky is a members/resort operation with access not confirmed.
rationale.weather: 4/5: NOAA 1991-2020 July mean high for Vail is 76.7 F (1-2 F over the 75 F target), low 41.6 F, 10 precipitation days.

lodging.name: Antlers at Vail: Unit 104 (3BR) + a 1BR condo
lodging.kind: condo lodge, 2 separate condos in one building
lodging.quick_verdict: Two creekside condos in one Lionshead building; first-floor 3BR suits the parents.
lodging.configuration: Antlers at Vail, 680 Lionshead Place, about 150 yards from the Lionshead lifts, shops and restaurants (property site). 86-87 condos from studios to 4BR/4BA, each with a private balcony and gas grill; creekside heated pool, two stone hot tubs, sauna, fitness room. Unit 104: about 1,400 sq ft, first-floor corner on the east end, originally two 1BR condos combined; 3 bedrooms plus a semi-private bunk-bed nook, 2 bathrooms, fireplace, full kitchen, two 5x10 ft balconies beside Gore Creek and the bike path. Bed sizes, dining-table seats and entry steps not stated. Scott & Andrea take a separate condo: the booking engine sells it as the Platinum 'One Bedroom plus Bunk Beds' (680 sq ft, sleeps 4; the lodging page lists 16 Platinum and 9 Diamond 1BR + bunks plus 8 Platinum plain 1BRs, with bath count and bed types not stated), so one bedroom plus a bunk nook, not a plain 1BR; floor not chosen until booking. The lodging page says every condo has a private exterior entryway. Alternative if 104 is taken: a 3BR/3BA such as Unit 514 (about 1,500 sq ft, king/king/queen, large west balcony), but 514 has two levels inside, so stairs for the parents; or a 4BR/4BA (6 exist). Elevator: a 2022 property post describes the relocated elevator with landings on each floor; it is not in the amenity list. Rates on the SynXis engine; a specific unit (104) is requested by phone, 1-888-268-5377.

lodging.name: Lion Square Lodge: South 255, 257 & 261 (three connected condos)
lodging.quick_verdict: Built-in lock-off suites beside the gondola, but small rooms and no view.
lodging.configuration: Lion Square Lodge, 660 Lionshead Place, in the ski yard next to the Eagle Bahn Gondola. South 255/257/261 is 3 bedrooms, 4 bathrooms, sleeps 8, second floor, rented as one set: 'three connected condos.' Main condo 255: eat-in kitchen, living room with TV, a bedroom suite with its own bath, and a Murphy bed in the entry hall with a connected bath. 257 (one-bedroom suite) and 261 (studio) each have a kitchenette, TV and full bath; they are reached through the kitchen door of 255, and the lodge also rents 257 & 261 as 'two neighboring lock-off suites' (and each on its own), which implies each has its own door. No balcony and 'doesn't offer a view.' Seating counts, bed sizes and elevator not stated. Heated outdoor pool and hot tubs year-round; Trails End restaurant on site; daily housekeeping, central air, free parking. Booking is by request form, with no rates shown. Bigger alternative in the same lodge: South 750, 4BR/4BA on two levels with river and mountain views, plus a separate unit for Scott & Andrea.

lodging_backups.name: Manor Vail Lodge: 3BR condo + studio
lodging_backups.quick_verdict: Golden Peak condos with breakfast included; layout and elevator details are thin.
lodging_backups.configuration: Manor Vail Lodge, 595 Vail Valley Drive at Golden Peak, 'easy walking distance' to Vail Village, Betty Ford Alpine Gardens and the Ford Amphitheater (no minutes given). 90 residences; every unit has a full kitchen, gas fireplace and private balcony, plus a daily hot breakfast buffet. 2 heated outdoor pools, 4 hot tubs, fitness center; BioMed Spa on site. 3BR: about 1,400 sq ft, large living room with fireplace, dining area, balcony over Golden Peak. Studio: from 700 sq ft with separate living area. Beds, baths, floors, elevator and dining seats not stated by the lodge; contact 800.950.8245.

lockoff.basis: Separately booked studio condo; the accommodations page calls every residence a full condominium with its own kitchen and balcony. It does not state entrances or floor plans (fact-checker 2026-11-14: 'own door' not stated; separate-unit basis only).

lodging_backups.food_convenience: Walking distance to Vail Village restaurants per the lodge (minutes not stated); breakfast included daily.

animals.name: Vail Stables: guided trail rides
animals.what_you_do: Guided horseback rides on White River National Forest trails: Rocky Point 1 hr ($130), Bear Hollow 1.5 hr ($165, family), Dark Timber 2 hr ($220).
animals.why_memorable: Aspen groves and meadows above Vail, 8 minutes from Lionshead.
animals.booking_difficulty: Online, 48 hours ahead; groups of 10-20 need 14 days. 225 lb limit (240-260 for tall riders)

image.alt: Rider and horse at Vail Stables

animals.name: Beaver Creek Stables
animals.what_you_do: 1- and 2-hour trail rides, a 3-hour picnic ride, Beaver Lake ride and a sunset ride to Beano's Cabin with dinner.
animals.why_memorable: The Beano's Cabin dinner ride pairs a ride with a mountain dinner.
animals.booking_difficulty: Phone (970) 845-7770; summer schedule only, dates not stated

image.alt: Trail ride at Beaver Creek Stables

animals.name: Vail Stables: GOGA! Goat Yoga
animals.what_you_do: One-hour yoga class while trained goats climb on backs, nudge and nap on participants; guests can hold a baby goat.
animals.why_memorable: Genuinely hands-on goat contact; suits Aubrey, Andrea and Jenna.
animals.booking_difficulty: Online (FareHarbor), at least 48 hours ahead; Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri and some Sat at 9am

animals.name: Vail Stables: Happy G.O.A.T. Hours
animals.what_you_do: Drop-in goat yard with a beer garden and play area; guests feed the goats treats. Parent-led pony rides ($20) for kids under 60 lb.
animals.why_memorable: Pushy, friendly goats a mile from Vail Village; easy for the parents to sit and watch.
animals.booking_difficulty: Drop-in on select days, 11am-4pm; days not listed

animals.name: Paragon Guides: llama hike
animals.what_you_do: A guided family-paced hike in the Holy Cross or Eagle's Nest wilderness with pack llamas carrying the food and gear; llamas are not ridden, and whether guests lead or touch them is not stated on the operator page (June to early September).
animals.why_memorable: Hiking beside a llama string in the backcountry; a lunch version (Backcountry Llama Lunch) is offered.
animals.price_usd: $795 for the first 2 people + $95 each additional (12 and under $75); about $1,365 for 8, plus $100 transport
animals.booking_difficulty: Request form; $100 non-refundable deposit, 72-hour cancellation; 970.376.7868. Office in Edwards; meeting point not stated

golf.name: Vail Golf Club
golf.what_you_do: 18 holes, par 71, 6,739 yards along Gore Creek; municipal and open to the public.
golf.why_memorable: Gore Range and White River National Forest views, with beaver ponds in play, 8 minutes from Lionshead.
golf.price_usd: Green fee not published on the club page (2027 rates page linked); rental clubs $69 for 18
golf.booking_difficulty: Online tee times; July is peak season

image.alt: Aerial of Vail Golf Club in summer

golf.name: EagleVail Golf Club
golf.what_you_do: 18 holes, par 71, Devlin/Von Hagge design at 7,650 ft; Stone Creek and the Eagle River come into play on 12 holes.
golf.why_memorable: Creek and river in play on 12 holes with Rockies views; a lower-key alternative.
golf.price_usd: Not published on the home page
golf.booking_difficulty: Online tee times (Club Caddie); public access not stated

activities.name: Gondola One and Eagle Bahn scenic gondola rides
activities.details: Both gondolas run in summer from Vail Village and Lionshead (2025: daily June 13-Sept 1, 9:30am-4pm); wheelchair and stroller accessible. 2027 dates and prices not published; Vail.com could not be loaded.

activities.name: Betty Ford Alpine Gardens
activities.details: Gardens near Vail Village with accessible paths, a 100-ft waterfall, an indoor Alpine House and a Children's Garden; season May-September; admission not listed.

activities.name: Vail Farmers' Market & Art Show
activities.details: Sundays 9:30am-3pm on East Meadow Drive, mid-June to early October, 150+ tents; check-in day, July 4, 2027, is a Sunday. Smaller Meadow Market Thursdays 4-7pm. 2027 dates not yet posted.

activities.name: Spa day: RockResorts Spa at The Arrabelle
activities.details: 10,000 sq ft spa with relaxation lounge and steam room at 675 Lionshead Place, next door to Antlers; Discover Vail lists 11 other spas in Vail.

activities.name: Bravo! Vail and Vail Dance Festival at the Ford Amphitheater
activities.details: Summer orchestral and dance seasons at the Gerald R. Ford Amphitheater near Golden Peak; 2027 dates not on the tourism page.

activities.name: Mountain biking
activities.details: Mountain biking is listed by Discover Vail as a signature summer activity; trail and rental details not checked.

shopping_exploring: Lionshead and Vail Village are pedestrian shopping streets along Gore Creek; the Sunday farmers' market adds 150+ tents. Beaver Creek Village is a smaller plaza 20 minutes west.

restaurants.name: Blue Moose Pizza
restaurants.notes: New York-style pizza, dine-in or takeout, $5 lunch slice-and-soda special; family-oriented.

restaurants.name: Bart & Yeti's
restaurants.notes: Pub fare, families and groups welcome, patio.

restaurants.name: Tavern on the Square
restaurants.notes: Contemporary American, lunch and dinner, outdoor patio on Lionshead's square.

image.alt: Patio at Tavern on the Square

restaurants.name: Vail Chophouse
restaurants.notes: Steak and seafood, dinner, large deck in Lionshead.

restaurants.name: Sweet Basil
restaurants.notes: Michelin Guide recommended (Sept 2025); seasonal local cooking, about 130 seats; reservations open 30 days ahead and fill fast in season. Price range not stated.

restaurants.name: The Little Diner
restaurants.notes: Retro diner, breakfast all day and lunch; expect waits at busy times.

july.notes: NOAA 1991-2020 normals for the Vail station (8,239 ft), via Wikipedia's climate table. Cool nights; days with 0.01 in or more of rain are about 10 of 31.

logistics.airport: Eagle County Regional (EGE); Denver International (DEN) as a drive-in alternative

flights.den: The Denver six can drive I-70 to Vail, about 2 hours plus traffic, or fly United/United Express DEN-EGE (year-round).
flights.bay_area: United Express lists EGE-SFO as seasonal (season not stated; may be winter only); otherwise connect via DEN to EGE, or fly to DEN and ride with the Denver group.

logistics.car_needed: Not inside Vail, where villages are walkable and the in-town bus is free; yes for the stables, golf and the airport. One or two cars are enough.
logistics.notes: EGE is 37 miles from Vail (Wikipedia). Avon and Beaver Creek are 15-20 minutes west of Lionshead.

caveats: Lodging prices (2026-11-14, Jul 4-10, 2027): only Antlers is verified ($1,167/night before tax, advance purchase non-refundable; $1,351 flexible). Westin Riverfront is an estimate from substitute hotel suites ($1,488/night incl. resort fees); Beaver Creek Lodge's 3BR condo is not sold online; Lion Square was not quoted. Manor Vail's 3BR and studio were not offered for the dates, so it moved to the backups.
Every gathering room is a condo or villa living room; no table for 8 was confirmed.
Town elevation about 8,150-8,240 ft; check with the parents' doctors about altitude.
July 4 week is peak: Sweet Basil, tee times and stables book up.
Animal options are domestic animals only (horses, llamas, goats); no wildlife or exotic-animal encounter found, and the Vail Nature Center was closed for summer 2026.
Red Sky Golf Club access for non-member guests not confirmed.
TripAdvisor blocked fetches and the web-search budget was exhausted, so the cross-check relied on Discover Vail.
